intervals.label: Phase I (PMT-only test-beam run)
intervals.note: Start month from the 2017 proposal (commissioned April 2016, data since May 2016); the end year is from the experiment page ("Phase I ... was successfully completed in 2017").
intervals.quote: Phase I was approved by the PAC in Spring of 2015, commissioned in April 2016. The collaboration has been taking data since May of 2016.

intervals.label: Phase II installation and commissioning
intervals.note: Month precision for the installation; the Fermilab feature of 11 March 2020 reports the first neutrino events in the Phase II detector, with gadolinium doping complete and source calibration under way.
intervals.quote: Phase II detector for the full physics program of the experiment was installed in July 2019 and data taking was started in 2020.

intervals.label: Phase II data taking
intervals.note: Open-ended: the 2025 LAPPD paper reports beam-correlated data in the running experiment; no source consulted says ANNIE has stopped.
intervals.quote: Phase II detector for the full physics program of the experiment was installed in July 2019 and data taking was started in 2020.

placements.note: Campus-grade Fermilab main-campus point reused; the SciBooNE hall has no separate coordinate in the sources read (the hall is 30 m deep per the Fermilab feature).

total_mass.quote: is a 26-ton water-based neutrino detector at Fermilab on the Booster Neutrino Beam (BNB)

summary.plain: A tank of gadolinium-doped water viewed by photomultiplier tubes and a few fast LAPPD light sensors, with a veto in front and an iron-scintillator muon tracker behind, in an underground hall.
summary.technical: Instrumented tank with 25 t Gd-loaded water as neutrino target and neutron tagger, 8-inch PMTs plus LAPPDs, a front veto against dirt-induced events and an iron-scintillator muon range detector; located in the SciBooNE hall.

technology.quote: The ANNIE experiment consists of a small Water Cherenkov detector, instrumented with both conventional photomultiplier tubes (PMTs) and Large Area Picosecond Photodetectors (LAPPDs) deployed on the Booster Neutrino Beam (BNB) at Fermilab.
technology.value: Gadolinium-doped water Cherenkov detector with PMTs and LAPPD fast photodetectors and a muon range detector
